page: Microsoft Azure D48lds_v5 is a compute-focused instance within the general purpose Dldsv5 family, provisioned via Microsoft Hyper-V. The server is powered by an Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor running on x86_64 architecture with a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz. It is configured with 48 dedicated virtual CPUs across 24 physical cores utilizing hyper-threading. The CPU includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache, with instruction support including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, VAES, and SHA-NI.

The instance is equipped with 96.0 GB of system memory, yielding a compute-oriented allocation of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Storage architecture features 1933 GB of local solid-state drive (SSD) storage capable of supporting high-throughput scratch disks or local caching layers. There are no discrete graphical processing units attached to this instance, and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default.

Benchmark testing illustrates reliable mid-tier multi-threaded and single-threaded compute output, with PassMark CPU scoring at 47311.76 and multi-core Geekbench reaching 15804.0. Stronger performance tiers appear in cryptographic and data-decompression tasks, shown by multi-threaded bzip3 decompression achieving 218.81 GB/sec and PassMark encryption scoring 41963.43. While small-model LLM generation reaches 269.44 tokens per second, large 70B language model inference drops significantly to 2.75 tokens per second due to the lack of dedicated acceleration and memory-bound scaling.

Cost efficiency is favorable for parallel computing environments where heavy storage I/O and CPU throughput take priority over high RAM per core. Tradeoffs center on the reduced 1:2 memory ratio and the degradation in large-parameter language modeling. Microsoft Azure D48lds_v5 is well matched for batch image processing, software compilation pipelines, multi-threaded compression tasks, local scratch storage databases, and high-concurrency microservices.
description: Microsoft Azure D48lds_v5 is a compute-aligned server instance featuring an Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system provides 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 24 physical cores, paired with 96.0 GB of RAM to deliver a 2.0 GB per core ratio. Local storage consists of a 1933 GB solid-state drive, while graphics processing units are absent. Benchmark evaluations indicate balanced general computing alongside strong results in cryptographic hashing, image processing, and multi-threaded decompression workloads like bzip3. Memory bandwidth reaches 155.55 GB/sec on large read blocks. The reduced memory-to-vCPU ratio presents a tradeoff for large in-memory footprints, but provides resource density for multi-threaded processing. The server is well suited for batch data processing, continuous integration compilation jobs, cryptography pipelines, and caching layers requiring high-capacity fast local disk.
